## Summary last lecture

-   Introduction to R
-   What are objects and functions?
-   Basic summaries of data
-   Different data types

## Tidy data {.small}

::: incremental

-   A **variable** is a quantity, quality, or property that you can measure. 
*Example: Flipper lenght*


-   A **value** is the state of a variable when you measure it. The value of a variable may change from measurement to measurement. *Example: Flipper lenght penguin 1 = 181 mm*

-   An **observation** is a set of measurements made under similar conditions. An observation will contain several values, each associated with a different variable. *Example: one row in penguin data for bill length, flipper length, body mass, etc. of one penguin*

-   **Tabular data** is a set of values, each associated with a variable and an observation. Tabular data is tidy if each value is placed in its own “cell”, each variable in its own column, and each observation in its own row.
:::



## Tidy data {.small}

::: incremental

1.  Each variable must have its own column

2.  Each observation must have its own row

3.  Each value must have its own cell

![](images/tidy_data.png){.fragment}


:::

## R functions

Functions take *arguments* as input. They can be named:

```{r}
#| echo: true

mean(x = penguins$bill_length_mm)

```

::: med-space
:::

Or unnamed:

```{r}
#| echo: true

mean(penguins$bill_length_mm)

```

## Why visualize?

::: med-space
:::

::::: columns
::: column
### Raw Data

```{r}
datasaurus_dozen %>%
  select(-dataset) %>%
  head(15) %>%
  gt() %>%
  gt_theme_pff()
```

:::

::: column
### Summary

```{r} 
datasaurus_dozen_dino <- datasaurus_dozen %>%
  filter(dataset == "dino")

c(
  `X Mean` = mean(datasaurus_dozen_dino$x),
  `Y Mean` = mean(datasaurus_dozen_dino$y),
  `X SD` = sd(datasaurus_dozen_dino$x),
  `Y SD` = sd(datasaurus_dozen_dino$y),
  Corr = cor(datasaurus_dozen_dino$x, datasaurus_dozen_dino$y)
) %>%
  enframe(name = "metric", value = "value") %>%
  gt() %>%
  fmt_number(columns = value, decimals = 2, use_seps = FALSE) %>%
  tab_options(
    data_row.padding = px(1),
    table.font.size = 44,
    table.width = "auto"
  ) %>%
  gt_theme_nytimes() %>%
  tab_options(column_labels.hidden = TRUE) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_body(columns = metric)
  )

```


:::
:::::

```{r} 
  head(28) %>%
```

## Mapping data to aesthetics {auto-animate="true" auto-animate-easing="ease-in-out"}

::: med-space

::::: columns

```{r} 
penguins %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = body_mass_g, col = species)) +
  geom_point() +

```

## Examples: Only numeric values

```{r}
penguins %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = bill_length_mm)) +
  geom_histogram() +
  labs(
    x = "Bill Length (mm)",
    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 20)
```


## Examples: Only numeric values

::: med-space
:::


```{r}
penguins %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = bill_length_mm)) +
  geom_density() +
  labs(
    x = "Bill Length (mm)",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 20)
```

## Examples: Only categorical values

::: med-space
:::

```{r}
penguins %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = species)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "count") +
  labs(
    x = "Species",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 20)
```


## Examples: Numerical and categorical values

::: med-space
:::

```{r}
penguins %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = species, y = flipper_length_mm)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "summary", fun = "mean") +
  labs(
    x = "Species",
    y = "Flipper length (mm)"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 20)
```

## Examples: Numerical and categorical values

::: med-space
:::


```{r}
library(ggthemes)

penguins %>%
  ggplot(
    aes(x = species, y = flipper_length_mm, fill = species),
  ) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = .75, shape = 21) +
  geom_pointrange(
    stat = "summary",
    fun.data = mean_sdl,
    show.legend = F,
    shape = 21
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Species",
    y = "Flipper length (mm)"
  ) +
  scale_color_colorblind() +
  scale_fill_colorblind() +
  theme_classic(base_size = 20) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```
